judgements.referenceQuote: President and CEO, Walmart, Inc.In officeFebruary 2014 – January 2026Preceded byMike DukeSucceeded byJohn Furner
judgements.evidenceQuote: Carl Douglas McMillon (born October 17, 1966[1]) is an American businessman who was the president and chief executive officer (CEO) of Walmart from 2014 to 2026 when he retired.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states he was president and CEO of Walmart from 2014 to 2026 and retired, but it never states that John Furner succeeded him as CEO.

judgements.referenceQuote: led the company's Sam's Club division, from 2005 to 2009, and Walmart International, from 2009 to 2013
judgements.evidenceQuote: led the company's Sam's Club division, from 2005 to 2009, and Walmart International, from 2009 to 2013
judgements.rationale: Same fact with the same roles and date ranges; the claim also notes he first joined as a summer associate, which does not change the match.

judgements.referenceQuote: He began his Walmart career in 1984 as an hourly associate
judgements.evidenceQuote: He has worked at Walmart for more than 30 years, starting as a teenager unloading trucks for an hourly wage.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states he started as a teenage hourly associate unloading trucks, but it does not give the 1984 start date or the distribution centre detail.

judgements.referenceQuote: It invested heavily in people by increasing wages, expanding parental leave and funding education opportunities. Walmart also lowered its prices, built a large eCommerce business and embraced technology to improve customer and associate experiences
judgements.evidenceQuote: We're gonna make some changes in a few months that will create a situation where no Walmart associate in the United States makes federal minimum wage.
judgements.rationale: The dossier touches on wage changes and omnichannel retail (an interview about omnichannel retail), but it does not present Walmart's own account of the tenure recording increased wages, expanded parental leave, funded education, lowered prices, a large eCommerce business and the omnichannel shift as a single account.

judgements.referenceQuote: Doug also served on the boards of Business Roundtable and the Consumer Goods Forum
judgements.evidenceQuote: serves on the board of directors for the Consumer Goods Forum, the U.S.-China Business Council, and is a member of the Business Roundtable
judgements.rationale: The dossier covers Business Roundtable and Consumer Goods Forum membership and separately his Walmart board seat, but it omits the 31 January 2026 retirement tie-in and adds the U.S.-China Business Council, so the full scoped fact is not stated.

judgements.referenceQuote: McMillon attended University of Arkansas, where he graduated with a  Bachelor of Science in Business Administration in accounting in 1989
judgements.evidenceQuote: Doug graduated from the University of Arkansas with a bachelor’s degree in business administration, and a master’s degree in business administration from the University of Tulsa.
judgements.rationale: The dossier states both degrees and institutions but omits the 1989 award year and the accounting concentration.

judgements.referenceQuote: Doug McMillon is a lifelong merchant
judgements.rationale: The dossier records a merchant background, but it does not attribute the 'lifelong merchant' characterisation to Walmart's own page or flag it as self-reported.

judgements.referenceQuote: McMillon was born in Memphis, Tennessee,[5] and grew up in Jonesboro, Arkansas,[6] the eldest of three children born to Laura and Morris McMillon, a dentist who served in Vietnam
judgements.rationale: The dossier states he is originally from Jonesboro, Arkansas, but omits the Memphis birth, being the eldest of three children, and the family's move to Bentonville when he was 16.

overclaims.statement: He delivered substantial growth in sales and earnings and transformed the brick-and-mortar retail giant into a digital powerhouse.
overclaims.citedQuote: He delivered substantial growth in sales and earnings and transformed the brick-and-mortar retail giant into a digital powerhouse as well.
overclaims.rationale: The cited HBR passage is a summary framing; attributing company-wide sales/earnings growth and digital transformation solely to McMillon personally overstates individual execution versus organizational output during his tenure.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is the CEO of Walmart.
overclaims.rationale: The claim asserts current CEO status, but McMillon retired in January 2026 and John Furner succeeded him; the cited quote ('CEO Doug McMillon') is from an older source and does not support present-tense currency.

overclaims.citedQuote: An interview with Walmart CEO Doug McMillon
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense claim contradicted by the January 2026 retirement; the cited interview title predates the retirement and cannot support current status.

overclaims.citedQuote: CEO Doug McMillon is leading the charge
overclaims.rationale: Asserts current CEO role; McMillon stepped down in January 2026, so the CBS quote ('CEO Doug McMillon is leading the charge') is stale as a description of his present role.

overclaims.statement: Forty years later, he’s Walmart’s president and CEO, a role he’s held for more than a decade.
overclaims.citedQuote: Forty years later, he’s Walmart’s president and CEO, a role he’s held for more than a decade.
overclaims.rationale: States present-tense presidency/CEO role; he retired in January 2026, so the Stanford quote no longer supports current status.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is a current member of Walmart's board of directors.
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug McMillon, former president and CEO of Walmart
overclaims.rationale: The cited quote itself says 'former president and CEO of Walmart,' which contradicts the claim's assertion of a current board seat; currency is not supported by the passage.

overclaims.statement: We're gonna make some changes in a few months that will create a situation where no Walmart associate in the United States makes federal minimum wage.
overclaims.citedQuote: We're gonna make some changes in a few months that will create a situation where no Walmart associate in the United States makes federal minimum wage.
overclaims.rationale: This is a forward-looking company policy statement ('we') about organizational action, not a personal act by McMillon; presenting it as his individual accomplishment overstates personal execution versus company output.

overclaims.statement: Led Walmart's acquisition of Jet.com to build e-commerce marketplace and capabilities
overclaims.rationale: The cited quote is only 'we bought Jet.com' — a collective company action; framing it as McMillon personally leading the acquisition and its strategic purpose goes beyond what the passage supports.

overclaims.statement: Unified supply chain aspects in 2020 to integrate buying and merchandising
overclaims.rationale: The quote 'unified the supply chain aspects' is a brief self-reported remark without clear personal attribution of the integration work; the claim's specificity (2020, integrating buying and merchandising) exceeds the passage.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon serves as CEO of Walmart.
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug McMillon, CEO of Walmart International, would replace Mike Duke as Walmart CEO effective on February 1, 2014
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense 'serves as CEO' is contradicted by the January 2026 retirement; the cited quote describes the 2014 succession announcement, not current status.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is president and CEO of Walmart Inc.
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug McMillon is president and CEO of Walmart Inc.
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense claim; McMillon retired as CEO in January 2026, so the cited biographical line is stale as a description of his current role.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is the president and chief executive officer of Walmart Inc
overclaims.citedQuote: Doug McMillon is the president and chief executive officer of Walmart Inc
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense claim contradicted by the January 2026 retirement; the change.org biographical line predates it.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon is the CEO of Walmart.
overclaims.rationale: Present-tense claim; the cited quote is just his name and cannot support current CEO status given the January 2026 retirement.

overclaims.statement: Doug McMillon served as CEO of Walmart.
overclaims.citedQuote: Before stepping down as CEO in January, Doug McMillon led Walmart
overclaims.rationale: Past tense 'served' is actually consistent with retirement, but the claim lacks the end date and could imply ongoing relevance; however, the cited quote ('Before stepping down as CEO in January') does support the past-tense framing. Marking uncertain rather than a clear overclaim.
